open_points.subject: A11 rule 1 authority step vs A10 scope of approvals
open_points.text: A11 rule 1: "Reaching an operation element runs in this order: ... then the authority of A10 rule 1, checked as it stands now — without it the element waits for approval"; A10 rule 1: "Before sending a `state-transition`, `external-effect` or `destructive` node, the kernel needs one of..." and "`draft-write` nodes ask nothing at run time".
open_points.question: Does the A11 authority/wait-for-approval step apply to `read` operations (and normal `draft-write` sends), or only to classes that A10 says require approval/grant authority?
options: Apply A11 authority check to every operation node, so even `read` can wait for approval.
Apply A11 authority check only to operation sends covered by A10 authority requirements; `read` never waits for approval and `draft-write` waits only in the resend-after-`not_applied` exception.
open_points.default_guess: Apply authority checks only where A10 requires them.

open_points.subject: Capture failed execution eligibility after run end
open_points.text: State 0 action "capture a failed execution into the trial corpus" refuses "an execution that succeeded, was skipped, belongs to another contract version, or whose run was already released (its files are gone)"; A15 rule 5 says capture "is allowed only while its run still holds its spool — the run has not ended, or ended `failed` and was not released — and is refused otherwise".
open_points.question: Is capture from a failed node in an ended non-`failed` run (for example `refused`/`cancelled`) always refused, even if needed inputs are non-file values, or should refusal depend only on the specific State 0 conditions?
options: Use A15 strictly: only not-ended or ended-`failed`-not-released runs are capturable.
Use State 0 failure list strictly: allow capture unless the listed refusal conditions occur.
open_points.default_guess: Use A15 strictly and refuse capture once a run ended other than unreleased `failed`.
